elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted paragraph: "Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates..." — an express defence obligation running to Customer and its Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: "...hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs, and expenses..."

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "Vendor's breach of Applicable Law", using the defined term in Section 1.2.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Limb (d): "Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: "Customer shall give Vendor prompt written notice of the claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: "Vendor shall control the defence" — control expressly allocated.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1 as rendered: Customer indemnifies Vendor "from third-party claims to the extent arising out of Customer-provided content or Customer's breach of Applicable Law", replacing the prior "every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services".

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Same inserted limb (a) covering allegations that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no modification exclusion was inserted, and the broader (unexcluded) indemnity is more favourable to Customer, so the permission is not violated.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no combination exclusion added and none is required, leaving the indemnity broader than the fallback floor.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no specification exclusion added, which does not defeat the fallback.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: No procure/modify/replace remedy appears anywhere in the rendered language; Section 9.3's reference to "the remedies required by Section 20.5" has no operative counterpart.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-of-fees fallback remedy is stated in the inserted indemnity or elsewhere in Section 20.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3x annual Fees super-cap was added; Section 21.3 leaves indemnification obligations as uncapped Excluded Claims, which is more favourable but does not satisfy this element.

elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Not a fallback element as such, but the fallback IP indemnity is supported by the same express "shall defend" language.

reasons: Preferred checklist is complete: all four indemnity triggers (IP infringement of Services/Deliverables, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), the express defend obligation to Customer and Affiliates, the full notice/control/cooperation procedure, and the narrowed Customer indemnity are all present in operative text, not merely promised in the comment.
Fallback is incomplete (no procure/modify/replace remedy, no refund fallback, no 3x annual Fees super-cap), but position-completeness only requires one level, and the preferred level is met.

Declining the 3x super-cap is defensible on the record: Section 21.3 already carves indemnification obligations out of the liability cap as Excluded Claims, so volunteering a cap would be a customer-adverse extra and would itself risk a minimality failure.

Minimality holds: the edit narrows Section 20.1 only to the two permitted Customer-indemnity triggers (required by element 10) and inserts a concise Vendor indemnity for a missing clause. No survival tail, at-own-expense wording, additional damages categories, or unrelated boilerplate was added, and no favourable existing language was deleted.

Intent preserved: the Excluded Claims definition, the Fees carve-out in Section 21.3, and the Section 9.3 termination triggers all survive without contradiction. The dangling cross-reference in Section 9.3 to "Section 20.5" pre-dates the redline and is not created by it.

Repair recommendations for the next turn (not defects in the checklist): (i) number the inserted paragraph (e.g., 20.2) so it is citable and so Section 9.3's reference to the infringement remedies can be conformed; (ii) if the Agreement does not define "Affiliate", change "Affiliates" to lowercase "affiliates" to avoid an undefined capitalised term; (iii) consider adding the Section 9.3 procure/modify/replace/refund remedies so the pre-existing cross-reference resolves — that would also close the fallback gaps at no cost.
